docs (LOW): CLAUDE.md, section 'Cost scanners — token semantics differ per source', documents the Claude dedup rule by message.id + requestId. It has no matching note for the new Codex rule that a token_count event whose total_token_usage did not change is skipped, and no note that all scanners share the CostWindow definition (today plus the six previous local days). Nothing there is wrong today, but it is the invariant section future edits rely on.

performance (LOW, route to performance lens): KeyedUsage.usage (ScanMemo.swift:79) now builds a ModelUsage on every read. It is called per record in ClaudeSessionScanner.fold/mergeKeyed on every scan. The cost is small and has no heap allocation unless boxed, but it is a CPU-for-memory trade the diff introduced.

OpencodeScanner.scan(providerGroups:) (Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cost/OpencodeScanner.swift:62-120) returns the same nil for four different causes: missing database, open/prepare/step failure, cancellation and a duplicate alias. Its doc comment says nil means 'opencode isn't installed', which is not accurate. CostEstimator.swift:76 therefore has to repeat the fileExists probe to tell a failure apart from 'not installed'. Proposal: return a result that names each case, so the caller does not have to re-check the filesystem. This is pre-existing; the fix did not introduce it.

AnalyticsAggregator.swift:81-84 measures 'Week' with rolling `7 * 86_400` steps, while the cost scanners now use CostWindow (today plus six local calendar days). In the Week tab, usage share and cost share can cover slightly different spans. Check whether they should be aligned. This is out of scope for the batch.
Small point: CostWindow (Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cost/CostWindow.swift:269) is `public` but only Core uses it. `internal` would be enough.

Test run: the full filtered suite passed (99 tests, 12 suites) on the fixed tree. The reversal was done by copying the files into the scratchpad, mutating them and restoring. Afterwards `git diff HEAD` is byte-identical to reviews/diffs/B2-scanners.diff. Minor note, out of scope: CodexSessionScanner Info.Usage now decodes total_token_usage. If that object ever carries a non-integer field, the whole token_count line would be counted as a decodeFailure instead of being billed. A lenient decode of total_token_usage (try? on that key only) would keep the dedup from affecting billing.
